### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **42** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`
- **41** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f75968bd98a9bb8bc54965d34d78180ccc2aab79` — the merge of head `3228b5954be2baccd7319e70a3d0f637f1e641a0` into base `d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f75968bd98a9bb8bc54965d34d78180ccc2aab79 && git checkout f75968bd98a9bb8bc54965d34d78180ccc2aab79
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7 3228b5954be2baccd7319e70a3d0f637f1e641a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7 && git merge --no-ff 3228b5954be2baccd7319e70a3d0f637f1e641a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d206d08cab87f4df16be918a231a3cc657e2bfe7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3228b5954be2baccd7319e70a3d0f637f1e641a0`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-13T04:36Z, adversarially, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Inputs: card #15953 (body and all 26 comments: the classification table `6115219467` row 9, the slice 5 claim `6135014332`, the dev report `6137873343`, the seat's ACCEPT `6138184218` read as a claim, and slice 4's records `6131842119` / `6134145854` on PR #23091 as the precedent); PR #23150's body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/23150/head` against merge base `0d43004100` (9 files, +1820 / -9, 7 commits including one merge of `origin/main`); the check-runs on the head, read twice. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the only local commands were `git fetch` / `git diff` / `git show` / `git log` / `git merge-base` / `git ls-tree` against the fetched ref, the template print, `gh api` reads, and reads of untouched spec, core, analytics, REST, lint and harness files at the head for the seams the family names.

### ① Derived judgments

**The three functions and twelve types, reachable and coherent: right.** `packages/verify/package.json` maps `.` to `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts` (and the `require` pair); `packages/verify/src/index.ts` exports `deriveDashboardWindowCases`, `runDashboardWindowProofs`, `formatDashboardWindowReport` and exactly the twelve types the changeset lists from `./dashboard-window.js`; the index diff is additive (the header count "Six" to "Seven" and the new block; nothing else moved). The shapes follow the siblings: `deriveXCases(config)` / `runXProofs(stack, token, config, options)` / `formatXReport(report)`, the token taken as the CRUD, reference-shape, delete-behaviour and unique-scope families take it; `app` is the same expression; `summary.hardFailures` is `contradicted + failed` widgets, and README, `cli.mdx` and the changeset each say so. The gate only ever reads what the run measured: `proven` needs every probed measure to hold under every preset, after the unwindowed control leg counted every fixture row; `inconclusive`, `unbound` and `excluded` are reported and not counted. Promises no more than measured, with one docblock hazard on a public type: `DashboardWindowProofOptions.now` says "The reference instant the ground truth resolves on" — literally true, but the server resolves the same tokens on its own clock (`resolveSelectionTokens`, `new Date()` per request), so a `now` that is not the current instant makes every window read `contradicted`. Nothing in the suite passes it. Owed one docblock sentence (pass the current instant or nothing) or the option's removal, on the next push to this file. Not a FAIL: it defaults right and no document advertises pinning the run.

**`os verify --dashboard-windows`: right.** `Flags.boolean` with `default: false`, typed into `runVerification`. With the flag, `bootStack(config, { multiTenant, hostRoot })` is a fresh stack stopped in `finally`, `signIn()` is the principal, `dashboardWindows.summary.hardFailures` is added under `?? 0`, the report rides `emitJson` (a `JSON.stringify`, so an `undefined` value emits no key), and the text branch is `if (dashboardWindows)`. Without the flag nothing moves but help text (the description, one `examples` row, one flag), a widening the minor carries. `packages/cli/test/verify-dashboard-windows.test.ts` spawns the real process and pins it: no `dashboardWindows` key and exit 0 without the flag; `proven`, 13 probes, 13 held, exit 0 with it; `contradicted`, inert, `hardFailures` 1, exit 1 on the same app plus its own window-dropping plugin, composed through `defineStackSourceFromLiteral`, so the spawned path carries the same control the library suite does.

**Where each expectation comes from: right, with two restated consumer rules named and immaterial to the door-scoped claim.**
- *The binding.* Every dashboard is `DashboardSchema.safeParse`, every dataset `DatasetSchema.safeParse`; the field is `filterBindings.dateRange` (string = that field, `false` = `unbound`, absent = `dateRange.field || 'created_at'`), resolved against `dataset.object` as the booted registry holds it (`stack.metadata.object`, system columns injected, so `created_at` resolves) and refused unless `date` / `datetime`. The spec's `dateRange.field` is `z.string().optional()`, and the `'created_at'` default lives in `DashboardWidgetSchema.filterBindings`' docblock and nowhere else: the lint's own copy (`validate-widget-bindings.ts:604`) says it "MUST track objectui `dashboard-filters.ts`", i.e. the default is applied by the console, not by any server. The family therefore applies a CONSUMER rule, sourced to the spec's docblock, which is the only in-repo statement of it; a third copy (lint, objectui, verify). The dev names it and the remedy (a spec export) is outside this claim. An empty-string `field` falls to the default, the lint's reading too.
- *What a preset hands the door.* `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` for each of the 13 `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS`, handed as the token pair `{ $gte: start, $lte: end }` (`$lte` absent for the three rolling presets), never lowered. The server's `resolveSelectionTokens` (`dataset-executor.ts:118`) resolves `selection.runtimeFilter` with `filterTokenContextFrom(context, new Date())` into core's `resolveFilterTokens`, the same function the family calls with `{ now: start, timezone, userId }` for the ground truth; `{today}` and its kin spell `YYYY-MM-DD` (`asYmd`), and `{current_user_id}` resolves to `context.userId`, the principal the family holds. Read from source, not re-derived.
- *The day boundary.* The ground truth compares a fixture's day with the resolved pair by the table's own convention (first and last day inclusive, the rolling end open); the engine compiles a bare-day `$lte` on a datetime column as strictly-before `nextUtcCalendarDay(day)` (`calendar-day.ts`, ADR-0053 D-D), which on a `date` column is order-equivalent to at-or-before the day, so a noon stamp on the last day is in both. The convention is restated as a string comparison rather than read from an engine helper; right for a ground truth, which must not be the engine checking itself, and the convention is the table's published text.
- *The `$and` composition.* `mergeFilters` appears in this repo only as objectui facts (`packages/spec/liveness/report.json`, the 2026-06 report-liveness audit): a restated consumer rule. What this repo publishes is the door's own composition, `combineFilters(compiled.filter, selection.runtimeFilter)` → `{ $and: [a, b] }` (`dataset-executor.ts:151-157`, applied at `:1113`), with measure filters applied per measure pass. It does not matter for the claim: the property measured is the door's count under a conjunction of the widget's filter and the window, every conjunction spelling selects the same rows, and the console's spelling is a sibling-repo fact the family cannot measure. README, `cli.mdx` and the changeset scope the promise to `POST /analytics/dataset/query`, so the claim is as narrow as the measurement.

**The door, and the attribution: sound.** `POST {basePath}/analytics/dataset/query` resolves `body.datasetName` through `p.getMetaItems({ type: 'dataset' })` and answers 404 on an unknown name (`rest-server.ts`), parses the selection through the door parse, and runs `queryDataset` under the request's `ExecutionContext` — the request a dashboard widget makes, as the signed-in principal. A plain member refused `403` reading the object is the dev's measurement, consistent with #16645's object-level read grant on this door; taking the caller's token is the sibling families' construction. Every count is `after − before` under the same window, so the app's own rows cancel; the control leg (`unwindowed.answered === written.length`) gates every window and also catches a concurrent writer or a misread measure key; the stamp and every held column are read back through the system read and compared with coercion tolerance (`sameValue`), a rewritten or omitted column making the probe `not-run`; a non-UTC principal timezone, a refused unwindowed query, a refused fixture and a required relation that cannot be seeded are each `not-run`; a day turning between `day0` and the after-queries is `not-run`. Under those gates a count that differs from the truth is attributable to the window. The two negative controls go through the engine's published seam (`registerMiddleware` with `{ object }`, `op.operation === 'aggregate'`, `op.ast.where`), no engine source changed, and the ablations of `judge` red exactly their controls as reported. ONE GAP, red-direction: the presets are resolved once at `start` (`options.now ?? new Date()`), but `day0` is read per measure and the fixture days are placed on `day0`; a run that crosses UTC midnight between `start` and a measure's probe judges that measure against yesterday's resolved edges while the server resolves today's, and reads `contradicted` (for example `last_7_days`: expected the days at or after the stale start, answered one fewer). The guard compares `todayAt(new Date())` with `day0`, never with `todayAt(start)`. A false RED in a rare window, never a false green; the documented class ("the day turned mid-probe") names it but the guard does not fully cover it. Owed a one-line guard (`day0 !== todayAt(start)` → `not-run`) on the next push to this file. Not a FAIL.

**The exclusions: excluded, not modelled.** `holdColumns` returns a reason for every `$`-operator key (`$or` among them), a relationship path, a condition on the window field itself, a field the object does not declare, any condition other than a bare scalar, `$eq`, a non-empty `$in` (first member), or `$nin` / scalar `$ne` on a field that declares options (first option not excluded; none left is a reason too), any placeholder other than `{current_user_id}`, a non-scalar value, and two holds that disagree. Measures: a derived measure, a non-count aggregate, a count of a relationship path. Widgets: an unparsed dashboard, an undeclared or unparsed dataset, an undeclared object (`sys_user`), an object the CRUD derivation cannot synthesize, a missing or non-temporal field judged on the booted registry. `unbound` is `filterBindings.dateRange === false` only. The derivation test and the booted test pin every kind with a count table (19 widgets: 10 proven, 1 unbound, 8 excluded by five kinds; 1 measure excluded beside a probed one).

**hotcrm: honestly scoped, read as reported.** No run was made here. The PR body states that the family measures count widgets only, that describe 2 also blank-checked three non-count widgets (`avg_resolution_time`, `sla_compliance_gauge`, `kb_deflection_rate`) which the family excludes and counts, that `daily_case_volume` is `unbound` where the file ran it windowless, and that the evidence came from direct runs over slice 3's artifact (protocol `^17.7.0` against this tree's 18, the 76 tombstones removed in memory), as slices 1-4 did. "0 contradictions with what describe 2 asserted" is true of what the family measured — the seven `case_count` widgets the file compared, plus three it did not, under all 13 presets, run C — and for the three non-count blank checks the family reports `excluded`, which is not the file's finding; the dev and the seat both name that residue. The 3 inconclusives of runs A and B (`is_closed` derived by hotcrm's own hook) are the attribution control on a real app. See ③ for the two standing notes.

**Docs sentences against the diff: right.** Changeset: three functions, twelve types (counted against `index.ts`), the signature `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack, token, config, { now? })`, the three sources, the fixture rule (smallest record, then every synthesized field — `fixtureBody(full)` and the one retry), the six statuses with each `inconclusive` arm matching a `notRun` site, the `excludedKind` list, the held-column rule, `hardFailures`, and the CLI paragraph ("without the flag the run and its document are unchanged") all match `dashboard-window.ts` and `verify.ts`. README: "Seven app-agnostic proof families" (index.ts says seven), the bullet, the opt-in paragraph, the exit-code sentence (`contradicted` or `failed`), the status table (six rows matching `widgetStatus` plus `unbound` and `excluded`), the API line. `cli.mdx`: the example row, the paragraph in the `os verify` section only, and the `--json` key list with `dashboardWindows` ("its `presets` name what each preset handed the door and how it resolved" — `condition` and `resolved`, true). The merge `3228b5954b` carried only main's own additions on `cli.mdx` and the README (#23093's sentence, present verbatim at the head) and the PR's own lines are byte-identical before and after it.

**The `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows: true of the code — and there are TWO, on three lines.** `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack: VerifyStack, ...)` and `formatDashboardWindowReport(report: DashboardWindowReport)` are exactly the gate's candidates (parameter 0 annotated with a package type re-exported as a type), `VerifyStack` being the concrete handle `bootStack` returns and `DashboardWindowReport` a value this package produced; `deriveDashboardWindowCases(config: any)` is not a candidate. The rows' words are the sibling rows' words; the dev's "2 problem(s)" before the rows agrees; `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:verify-stand-in`, is green on the head. The ACCEPT's "3 `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows" counts lines, not rows; harmless.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md`: `@objectstack/verify` **minor**, `@objectstack/cli` **minor**. The diff publishes three new functions and twelve new types from `@objectstack/verify` and one new opt-in flag plus help text from `@objectstack/cli`; no existing export, signature, default or behaviour moves (the `index.ts` and `verify.ts` diffs are additive; `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs` gains two ledger rows). Minor is the right level for both and meets the card's own acceptance ("`@objectstack/verify` minor per new exported family"). Not breaking, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` reading agrees, and `Check Changeset` is success on the head (both runs, the last after the seat's label write).

`Clause-②` carriers: PR body line 2 `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset body `Clause-②: yes`; the claim `6135014332` `Clause-②: yes`. The three agree. Each is legal: `yes` with no arm is a complete declaration, and `yes` takes at least minor, which both entries are.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6137873343`: `open_questions` empty. Its deviations and findings, each answered or escalated:

- **What a preset hands** (assumption 3): answered in ① — the spec's table is the in-repo statement of each preset's window; hotcrm's `{ $gte, $lte: '{today}' }` pair is the console's lowering, a sibling-repo table; over fixtures that never post-date today, with the differential, both select the same rows, so the verdict is the same under either. The divergence for future-dated rows is the class (b) finding below.
- **The door as the dev admin** (assumption 4): answered in ① — a member is refused reading the object; the caller's token is the sibling families' construction; the saved dataset resolves by name today, so nothing waits on #23088 (not landed at either reading; one composition measured).
- **The ground truth as a difference, the control leg, `$nin` / `$ne` on declared options, the one retry with every synthesized field** (assumption 5): answered in ① — each is a gate that keeps a non-window cause out of `proven`, and the retry is pinned by a fixture hook.
- **The negative controls through an app plugin's aggregate middleware** (assumption 8): answered in ① — the engine's published seam, composed identically by `bootStack` and the spawned CLI; no engine source changed.
- **Date fields included** (assumption 2): answered — `due_on` on the fixture app, `close_date` on hotcrm, the stamp taking the day itself, order-equivalent under the calendar-day rule.
- **Scratch files in slice 1's folder; two runs outliving the lock wrapper; the hotcrm clone left in place; commit trailers**: process notes. The head tree carries no scratch, pid or log file (`git ls-tree`), so Post-Task Checklist step 7 holds for the repo; the reported counts come from runs completed under the lock. Not contract matters.
- **One merge of `origin/main`; main moved six more commits**: answered in ① — the merge carried only main's own change; `f931e765b7` refines `DashboardHeaderActionSchema.actionUrl`, which the family's parse reads, and hotcrm's dashboards declare no header actions, so its counts cannot move; the net diff against the merge base is the nine files reviewed.
- **Out-of-scope finding, class (b), reach at a public door — the rolling presets' three extents. The evidence is sound as stated.** Read in source at the head: `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` hands `last_7/30/90_days` as `$gte`-only, and its docblock says in one breath that "the resolver's clock is the bound" and, for calendar presets, that `$gte` alone "selects every day AFTER the window on a column that carries future dates" — the second sentence is true of the rolling form too, since a `$gte`-only filter carries no clock at all; `bareDateRangePresetComparandMessage` prescribes that open form to authors at the save door and the lint; core's `resolveAnalyticsDateRangePreset` closes the same three presets at `now` (inclusive, `analytics-date-range.ts:189-193`); the console's `PRESET_RANGES` closing at `{today}` is the dev's read of objectui at the pin (sibling repo, not verified here). Three extents for one preset name, and the measured `2 / 1 / 1` on today−5 and today+5 is exactly what they predict. Under Prime Directive #10 that is a contract violation with a repro and an authoring trap (the prescription an author is handed selects a different extent than the picker it is prescribed for). It does not move the head: the family's fixtures never post-date today and the differential cancels an app's own future rows. ESCALATED: the seat takes it to the filing gate in this round, as the ACCEPT says; lane (spec's table and message, core's arm) and grade are triage's.
- **Finding, carrier none — the `created_at` literal**: a note is right; now three copies (lint, objectui, verify), each sourced to the same docblock; a spec export is the remedy, outside this claim. Not a defect under #10.
- **Finding, carrier none — `fixtureBody` / `vary` / `laterBy` / `uniqueFields` in four family modules**: slice 4's finding 5, one copy later; a refactor into `derive.ts`, outside this claim. A note is right.
- **Finding, carrier none — count widgets only.** A note is right for the family, and a STANDING NOTE for the card: row 9's D residue is "describe 2", and describe 2's blank check over three non-count widgets is not measured by this family (an average or ratio has no row-level ground truth without modelling the measured column). The card's acceptance clause "reports the same findings the retired hotcrm file asserted" is met for every count widget and not for those three. ESCALATED to the card: hotcrm's retirement of describe 2 keeps those three blank checks until a later slice measures them, or the card re-scopes them.
- **Finding, carrier none — hotcrm's `is_closed` hook** (runs A and B): the attribution control doing its job; slice 4's finding 4 class. No carrier.
- **Finding, carrier none — an `internal: true` window field**: the system read omits it and the door refuses it as a filter key, so such a binding reads `inconclusive` here and can only ever refuse at the door. A note is right; not this PR's.
- **The hotcrm clause ("runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata")**: this tree is protocol 18 and hotcrm pins `^17.7.0`, so the clause cannot be met on this tree for this slice either; the same open acceptance note slices 1-4 landed under. ESCALATED, not a FAIL: the card stays open for its remaining rows, and whoever closes it owes that clause a run or a re-scope.
- **Added by this review**: the midnight gap between `start` and `day0` (①), owed a one-line guard on the next push to `dashboard-window.ts`; the `DashboardWindowProofOptions.now` docblock (①), owed a sentence; the ACCEPT's row count (①), harmless. None is a carrier.

**Check-runs on the head, read three times in this act, the last at 2026-10-13T04:36Z, latest run per name.** 41 names; at the final read every run had concluded: 34 success, 7 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress (the ACCEPT's "36 success and 5 skipped" counts the two `labeled` re-runs' earlier successes as latest; same runs, different dedup). Success: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset` (the 04:23Z run after the seat's label write, success), `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (no governed path among the nine files; `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs` is not under `.claude/**`), `Lint & Repo Gates`, the eight `Lint ·` jobs, the four PR-shape guards, `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core` and its six shards, the four `Type Check ·` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check` and `filter`. Skipped: `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` on their 04:23Z `labeled` re-run (their 03:52Z runs on this same head were success), and the five roster skips on a PR run (`Console Pin Gate`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix row, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`), as slice 4's record found. No gate was re-run by this act. What the seat owes before the queue, none of it in this diff: the class (b) carrier, the two standing card notes, and the sequence the ACCEPT set (after #23148 clears); what the next push to `dashboard-window.ts` owes: the midnight guard and the `now` docblock sentence.
